card.title: Test the Story First
card.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask Dad why our holiday account's empty. I'll wait by the kitchen door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come with me. You booked the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask whether he's angry about the price first. If he isn't, I'll come in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm calling you in if he wants the flight receipt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask whether he wants the total or the breakdown before you call me. The seat upgrades need a longer explanation.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sends B inside while waiting; A3 makes entry depend on anger and A5 asks another probe before receipt disclosure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 A booked flights prompts A3 a price-reaction test; B4 receipt condition prompts A5 total-versus-breakdown testing.

relationship.evidence: B2 insists A share responsibility and B4 agrees only with a clear condition for involving A.

heightening.evidence: B4 threatens detailed evidence; A5 subdivides the test to postpone explaining seat upgrades.

specificity.evidence: A1 holiday account and kitchen door, B2 flights and A5 upgrades give concrete family spending stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 upgrades needing longer explanation earns the final delay from B4's receipt demand.
